extracted.intended_audience: Developers/contributors to the Conan C/C++ package manager repository (C/C++ package authors and project contributors).
extracted.subtask_description: Developer-facing README and contributor/test-run instructions for setting up, installing, and running tests for the Conan repository. Covers repository layout expectations, installation in editable mode, test requirements, environment variables, and guidance for contributors to add tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository directory name
rubrics_metrics.description: Repository directory name matters; some directories are known to be problematic to run tests (e.g. conan). conan-io directory name was tested and guaranteed to be working.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clone into a directory named conan-io to avoid known test/runtime issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install in editable mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Install Conan from source in editable mode using: cd conan-io && sudo pip install -e .
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On Windows, using sudo is not required. Some Linux distributions won't allow editable installs into the root Python installation — create and use a virtual environment first in those cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a Python virtual environment on non-Windows systems (or use sudo)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are not on Windows and you are not using a Python virtual environment, you will need to run these commands using sudo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editable installs or pip installs require root, create a virtual environment (venv) first and install there to avoid using sudo in the system Python.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify installation by running conan --help
rubrics_metrics.description: After installation you should verify Conan is runnable: $ conan --help
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a basic sanity check that the local installation succeeded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Add tests for contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you plan to contribute, please add some testing for your changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the contributing guide and the 'Conan tests guidelines' section for advice on how to write tests for Conan. Feedback and contribution are welcome but expected to include tests where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Install Python requirements for running tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Install test requirements with: python -m pip install -r conans/requirements.txt; python -m pip install -r conans/requirements_server.txt; python -m pip install -r conans/requirements_dev.txt
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not on Windows and not using a virtual environment, run these commands with sudo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set PYTHONPATH before running tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Before running tests set PYTHONPATH to include the repository root: export PYTHONPATH=$PYTHONPATH:$(pwd) (on Windows: set PYTHONPATH=.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run this while in the Conan root directory so tests can import the local package code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required external tools and versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some specific versions of external tools are necessary; for example, cmake>=3.15 is required for some tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test suite config (conftest.py) defines and configures required tools (CMake, Ninja, etc.). Ensure those tools meet minimum versions before running tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run tests with pytest; use -s to see output
rubrics_metrics.description: Run the test suite with: python -m pytest . A useful option is -s to see output that would otherwise be captured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can run specific tests by specifying the test file and test class/method, e.g. python -m pytest test/functional/command/export_test.py::TestRevisionModeSCM::test_revision_mode_scm -s. Example expected output after a full run is a test summary such as 'Ran 146 tests in 50.993s' followed by 'OK'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Running Artifactory-dependent tests requires special env vars and a separate server
rubrics_metrics.description: Some tests can be run against an instance of Artifactory; those tests should add the attribute artifactory_ready and require environment variables to be defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To run these tests, set CONAN_TEST_WITH_ARTIFACTORY=1 and provide ARTIFACTORY_DEFAULT_URL (base URL), ARTIFACTORY_DEFAULT_USER, and ARTIFACTORY_DEFAULT_PASSWORD. Running these tests will create repositories on the server — use a separate testing server.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project commitment to stability (do not break recipes/behavior)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stable. Used in production by many companies; since 1.0 there is a commitment not to break package recipes and documented behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contributors should be careful to avoid changes that break package recipes or documented behavior; maintain backward compatibility where expected by users in production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write extensible Python-based recipes and use extension points
rubrics_metrics.description: Conan is extensible: its Python-based recipes, together with extension points, allow for power and flexibility when producing packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing or contributing package recipes, prefer the established Python-based recipe patterns and extension points documented by the project for consistency and compatibility.
